narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 12 % chance you won’t pass your final year, which is just above the 10 % threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reasons the model reached this decision are tied to three key areas. First, the fact that you chose this school because of its reputation actually worked in your favor—it slightly reduced the risk of failing. Second, you’ve never failed a class before, which also helped lower the risk. Finally, your strong ambition to pursue higher education was another positive factor that pushed the prediction away from failure.

However, the model still flagged a small but important risk, largely because of your attendance. You’ve missed 21 days of school, which is much higher than the average of just 3 days among students who aren’t required to take remedial courses. This high number of absences was the biggest concern, as it suggests you may have missed critical lessons or fallen behind.

The remedial courses will give you a chance to catch up on what you’ve missed and strengthen your understanding of key subjects. Since you’re already motivated to continue your education, focusing on improving attendance and making the most of this support will help you stay on the path to success.
